corrected_value.title: Risk variants for atrial fibrillation on chromosome 4q25 associate with ischemic stroke

decisions.quote: At the 4q25 (PITX2) locus, previously identified by GWAS, we confirmed the association at rs2634074 with CE stroke (OR = 1.43 for the T allele; 95% CI, 1.13–1.81, p = 0.029), but not at rs2200733 (OR = 1.30 for the T allele; 95% CI, 0.96–1.76; p = 0.60) (Table 1).

Neurol., doi:10.1002/ana.21480) in the independent Dutch cohort for two specific associations of rs2200733 at 4q25 (PITX2): with overall ischemic stroke (previously reported OR 1.25 [1.15-1.37], p = 3.14 x 10^-7; Dutch cohort OR 1.11 [0.94-1.31], p = 0.90) and with cardioembolic (CE) stroke (previously reported OR 1.54 [1.33-1.78], p = 8.05 x 10^-9; Dutch cohort OR 1.30 [0.96-1.76], p = 0.60), whereas the other 4q25 SNP rs2634074 is explicitly mapped in Table 1 to Ref. 9 (Kilarski et al., 2014). corrected_value.title: Meta-analysis in more than 17,900 cases of ischemic stroke reveals a novel association at 12q24.12

decisions.quote: In a well-defined cohort of patients with IS, we confirmed the 4q25 (PITX2) and 16q22 (ZFHX3) loci to be significantly associated with the IS subtype CE. We also found locus 16q22 to be significantly associated with overall IS. We were not able to replicate the previously-established associations at the 1p13.2 (TSPAN2), 6p21.1 (SUPT3H/CDC5L), 7p21.1 (HDAC9), 9p21.3 (CDKN2B-AS1), 9q34 (ABO) and 12q24 (ALDH2) with overall IS or its subtypes although, barring locus 6p21.1 (SUPT3H/CDC5L), the effect direction of their associations were consistent with expectation2–11.
decisions.reason: Table 1, Results, and Discussion explicitly re-test Ref. 9 (Kilarski et al., 2014, Neurology, doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000000707) in the independent Dutch cohort for two specific associations: rs10744777 at 12q24 (ALDH2) with overall IS (previously reported OR 1.10 [1.07-1.13], p = 7.12 x 10^-11; Dutch cohort OR 1.01 [0.90-1.12], p = 1.00) and rs2634074 at 4q25 (PITX2) with cardioembolic (CE) stroke (previously reported OR 1.33 [1.24-1.42], p = 1.52 x 10^-16; Dutch cohort OR 1.43 [1.13-1.81], p = 0.0285 in Table 1 / 0.029 in text). Per review instructions, outcome is set to cannot_be_determined as outcomes are not requested in this identity review. This 2014 study is genuinely absent from all shipped rows: input_row_index 2412 is Bellenguez et al. (2012, doi:10.1038/ng.1081, Ref. 11 on HDAC9) and input_row_index 2504 is Holliday et al. (2012, doi:10.1038/ng.2397, Ref. 5 on 6p21.1), which are distinct studies of different loci, and it is also distinct from sibling targets Ref. 2 (NINDS SiGN 2015, which tests ALDH2 rs10744777 with SVD rather than overall IS) and Ref. 3 (Gretarsdottir et al. 2008, which tests PITX2 rs2200733 rather than rs2634074); thus report equivalence and duplicate target exclusion do not apply.
